extraction.name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
extraction.description: A new texture dataset spanning 246,285 images across 56 texture classes, generated using text-to-image models with a three-stage refinement process to ensure high quality, diversity, and alignment with prompts.
extraction.creator: Blaine Hoak, Patrick McDaniel
extraction.citeAs: Hoak, B., & McDaniel, P. (2025). On Synthetic Texture Datasets: Challenges, Creation, and Curation. arXiv:2409.10297v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were generated using Stable Diffusion model pipelines based on constructed texture-specific prompts. 5 images were generated per prompt, resulting in 483,840 images before refinement.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Images flagged as NSFW by the Stable Diffusion safety filter were excluded from the final dataset and not released publicly, despite containing no explicit content.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 483,840 images generated by Stable Diffusion before refinement.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A three-stage refinement process was applied to filter down the generated images: frequency analysis, patch variance filtering, and CLIP scoring.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: 1. Frequency filtering: Retained top 80% of images with highest frequency cutoff values to remove object-like features. 2. Patch variance filtering: Filtered out bottom 20% of images with lowest mean patch variance to eliminate homogeneous images. 3. CLIP score filtering: Filtered out bottom 20% of images with lowest CLIP scores to ensure prompt alignment.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 9 participants were recruited to evaluate images. Each participant was shown 100 images in random order and asked to rate (1-5) the overall quality and how well the image represents the provided descriptor.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each refinement step positively contributed to quality and representativeness, yielding a 3.4% increase in quality and a 4.5% increase in representativeness overall. Patch Variance and CLIP refinement contributed the most to the increases.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stable Diffusion, CLIP model, Fourier transforms
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Highlights the need for refined NSFW filters that can better handle abstract or texture-based content, as benign texture prompts often triggered safety filters.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Textures appearing in common objects (e.g., hairy, flaky) tend to have better quality scores, while structured textures (e.g., grid, polka-dotted) tend to have worse scores. The Stable Diffusion safety filter is biased against certain texture descriptors like 'paisley'.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: There is room for improvement in generating more structured textures. Descriptors like 'muted' often resulted in destroyed image quality. Symmetric images were sometimes not symmetric.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Interpreting high-level features models learn, uncovering biases, identifying security vulnerabilities, measuring texture bias (e.g., Texture Object Association Values).
